Core Concepts

is organized around a small set of stable concepts: , , Snapshots, and a deterministic streaming Pipeline. These concepts define the public contract surface for state ownership, state updates, and state consumption.

This page defines the minimal vocabulary and responsibilities you’ll use across all documentation and day-to-day development.

Core Building Blocks

Vault configuration defines system-level runtime defaults used by FeatureCells (for example, queue behavior and log settings). Vault is a configuration surface and does not define FeatureCell initialization, state access, or state update APIs.

A FeatureCell is a feature-scoped State container and the primary consumer-facing API surface. It defines a feature domain and exposes the consumer entry points for initialization, state access, and state updates, including replaceState() and mergeState().

State

State is immutable, feature-owned data managed by a FeatureCell. treats State updates as deterministic, ordered transformations rather than ad-hoc mutation.

Snapshot

A Snapshot is an immutable representation of State at a moment in time. Snapshots are the consumer-visible output of a resolution pass and are exposed through the FeatureCell output surface.

Best Practices

The FeatureCell (or the service/module that owns it) is the architectural boundary for state updates. UI components should not call Vault or state update APIs directly.

A recommended structure is:

  • Component → calls domain/service methods
  • Service/Module → invokes replaceState() or mergeState()

This preserves separation of concerns. Components remain focused on rendering and user interaction, while state ownership and mutation logic remain centralized and testable.

Lifecycle

FeatureCell interaction is consistent across features: the FeatureCell is initialized before state interaction, state updates enter the Pipeline, and Snapshots are produced as output.

FeatureCell output exposes a Snapshot wrapper suitable for UI consumption. Depending on the integration surface, Snapshot access is available as an Observable stream or as a Signal (angular only).

State Update APIs

State updates enter through two primary APIs:

replaceState

replaceState replaces the entire Snapshot for a FeatureCell. It is used when the new Snapshot should be considered complete.

mergeState

mergeState merges partial values into the existing Snapshot using the active Merge Behavior for the FeatureCell. The default Merge Behavior replaces arrays rather than merging them and passes through non-array values unchanged.

replaceState and mergeState Input

StateType defines the structured update payload accepted by both replaceState and mergeState. It represents an update intent rather than a complete Snapshot, allowing callers to specify only the portions of state they wish to change. Each field is optional, enabling partial updates while preserving immutability and deterministic processing through the pipeline.

Pipeline

The Pipeline is the ordered lifecycle through which State is resolved and emitted. Each Stage is an execution slot occupied by a Behavior. Pipeline ordering is deterministic.

Behaviors and Extensions

Behaviors are built-in (critical behaviors) and opt-in units that participate as Stages within the Pipeline. Behaviors may transform State, constrain emissions, constrain emissions, integrate storage, or expose consumer-facing Extensions.

Extensions are public APIs contributed by Behaviors that extend the FeatureCell’s fluent API without altering the core FeatureCell contract.

State Consumption

FeatureCells output exposes a Snapshot wrapper suitable for UI consumption. Depending on the integration surface, Snapshot access is available as an Observable stream or a Signal (angular only).

StateSnapshotShape defines the Snapshot fields used for consumption and rendering decisions, including loading, value presence, and error state.

Built-In Error Handling

provides a first-class, built-in error handling model that works at both the feature level and the application level.

Errors can be handled directly within a FeatureCell when the error is specific to that feature’s domain, or observed globally through the VaultErrorService when errors need to be monitored, logged, visualized, or reacted to across the entire application.

This dual-level approach allows teams to keep feature-specific error logic close to the feature itself, while still enabling centralized error reporting, analytics, and tooling without additional wiring or custom infrastructure.

All error normalization, propagation, and exposure is built into the system by default. Developers do not need to create custom error buses, global stores, or cross-cutting services to achieve consistent error handling.

User defined or pipeline errors are represented on the Snapshot as an immutable, normalized VaultErrorShape.
